## 2.1 Exploration

The well 25/6-1 was drilled on a prospect west of the main fault in
the southern part of the block.

The primary reservoir targets were the Middle Jurassic sandstone of
the Brent Group Equivalent and the Lower Jurassic sandstone of the
Statfjord Formation.

The Quaternary/Tertiary sequence is 2017 m thick, and is represented
by the Nordland, Hordaland, Rogaland and Montrose Groups.  The
Nordland Group consists of marine claystone with sands frequently
developed, especially in the lower part, with 163 m of the sandy
Utsira Formation.  The Hordaland Group consists of clay/claystone
with some thin sand units.  Slightly tuffaceous claystone is the main
lithology of the Rogaland Group, and the Montrose Group a sand/marl/
claystone sequence.

A 65.5 m thick Cretaceous sequence represented by Shetland and Cromer
Knoll Groups was penetrated.  The main lithology is chalky limestone,
calcareous claystone grading to marl and minor sand.

The Jurassic sediments represented by the Viking, Brent and Dunlin
Groups and the Statfjord Formation were encountered at 2233.5 m RKB.
The sequence is 269.5 m thick and consists of Upper Jurassic shale,
Middle Jurassic sandstones and alternating sandstones and silty
claystone in the lower part.

A 348 metres thick Triassic sequence represented by the Skagerrak and
Smith Bank Formations was penetrated.  The sequence consists of
shale/siltstone.

The well was drilled 30 m into Basement consisting of crystalline
rocks, probably of Late Paleozoic/Pre-Cambrian age.

Two cores were cut in the Brent and Dunlin Groups.

## 2.2    Operation

The drilling rig "Treasure Saga" arrived on the location December 16,
1985, and the well was spudded at 1700 hrs December 18.  The 36" hole
was drilled from 147 m RKB seabed to 260 m RKB.  The 30" casing was
run and cemented with the shoe at 255 m RKB.  The seabed diverter was
run on riser, landed and tested before drilling a pilot hole down to
1028 m RKB.  The hole was logged in one run and then opened to 26"
using an underreamer.  The 20" casing was run and cemented with the
shoe at 1013 m RKB.

The BOP was installed.

The 17 1/2" section was drilled, and from 1235 m RKB gumbo became a
continuous problem down to approx. 1400 m RKB.  A chalky formation at
2170 m RKB decreased the penetration rate, and it also caused
problems during tripping.  The section had to be reamed several
times, finally a soltex/diesel pill was pumped to stabilize the hole.

The 13 3/8" casing was run and cemented with the shoe at 2180 m RKB.
The 12 1/4" section was drilled down to T.D. at 2881 m RKB.  Two
cores were cut from 2289 m RKB to 2309.7 m RKB.  The section was
logged and the well was plugged back to 2360 m RKB in 3 steps.

The 9 5/8" casing was run and cemented with the shoe at 2355 m RKB.

One production test was carried out in the Brent Group Equ.

The casings were cut and the well plugged before leaving the location
at 0530 hrs February 3, 1986.

2.3    Formation Evaluation and Testing.

The upper part of the Brent Group Equ. (2277 - 2297 m RKB) was found
oil bearing with an OWC at 2282.5 m RKB. The net to gross ratio in
the Brent Group Equ. is 0.82, with an average porosity of 24.0%.
From the top of the reservoir to the OWC, the net to gross ratio is
0.75, with an average porosity and water saturation of 29.2% and 38%,
respectively.

The Statfjord Formation (2417.0 - 2503.0 m RKB) was found water
bearing with a net to gross ratio of 0.45 and an average porosity of
23.3%.

One production test was carried out in the Brent Group Equ. The
average production rate was 298 Sm3/day with a wellhead pressure of
96 bar and a choke size of 7.9 mm.

The PVT - analysis of reservoir fluid collected during the production
test, gives an oil formation volume factor of 1.92 Rm3/Sm3, a gas
to oil ratio of 232.2 Sm3/Sm3 and a stock tank oil density of
729 kg/m3. The bubble point pressure for the fluid is 106.9 bar.

## 4.1  Geographic and Structural Setting

The wildcat well 25/6-1 is located in the southern part of the block
on the northeastern side of the Utsira High.

At the Middle Jurassic level, there is a single closure defined by
the 2277 m MSL closing contour on the Top Brent depth map (fig. 4.1.).

## 4.2  Purpose of the Well

The purpose of the well was to test for hydrocarbons in the prospect
west of the main fault in the southern part of the block. The target
reservoir horizons were sandstones belonging to the Brent Group Equ.
which is partly eroded in this area, and the sandstones of the
Statfjord Formation.

In addition the Lower Tertiary sands were believed to represent a
secondary target.

The objective for the total depth was to drill through a strong
seismic reflector between 2.5 and 2.6 sec. TWT.

## 4.6 Well Velocity Survey

A zero offset VSP was acquired and processed by Geco Well Services.

A Bolt 1500-airgun, 286 cu. in. capacity, a Teledyne hydrophone and a

frequencies at 20, 25, 30, 35, 40 and 45 Hz. Synthetic seismograms
were produced for the frequency of a 35, 40 and 45 Hz Ricker
wavelet. All synthetic seismograms were displayed in both normal and
reverse polarity with both minimum and zero phase Ricker wavelets.

# 6.1    Operation

## 36" Section

The well was spudded December 18, 1985, using a 26" bit and a 36"
hole opener.

The measured depth from RKB to seabed was 147 m. The well was
drilled down to 260 m, pumping a high viscosity pill on every
connection. Seven surveys were taken in this section, the deviation
on the bottom was 1/2°.

After a wipertrip to seabed, another high viscosity pill was
circulated through the system before displacing the hole to 1.15 SG
gel-mud. Nine joints of 30" casing were run. The PGB was landed in
the TGB with 1 1/2° angle and the casing was cemented according to
programme with 30" casing shoe at 255 m.

## 26" Section

The seabed diverter was run on riser, landed, pressure and function
tested together with the rest of the diverter equipment.

The 30" casing shoe was drilled out with a 17 1/2" bit and 26"
underreamer. A 17 1/2" pilot hole was drilled down to 627 m before
doing a wiper trip, monitoring the formation continuously with the
MWD-tool to discover potential shallow gas pockets. During the wiper
trip, the beam on the monkey board holding the standlifter was
exposed to an accidentally high load, resulting in bending the beam.
While repairing the damage, it was necessary to stay with the bit
inside the shoe, circulating for 16.5 hrs.

The MWD-tool malfunctioned when going back on bottom and the
remainder of the section was drilled with conventional single shot
surveys every 100 m throughout this section. The surveys showed a
deviation between 0° and 1/2°.

## Testing

A 9 5/8" casing scraper and 8 1/2" bit were run on drill pipe to top
cement (2325 m). The mud was circulated and conditioned.

The test string was then run picking up the 5" VAM in singles filling
the string with a diesel cushion. The test string was pressure
tested at regular intervals while running in the hole. A dummy run
was performed with the fluted hanger. When the fluted hanger was
landed in the 9 5/8" wear bushing, a gamma ray-ccl log was run for
depth correlation. The test string was then pulled to the fluted
hanger and after installing the sub-sea test tree, the remainder of
the test string was run in the hole.

The packer was then set and the depth was correlated using a gamma
ray-ccl log tool. The well was then perforated using the Vann
systems pressure activated firing system (tubing pressure to activate
the firing system 310 bar).

After perforating, the well was backsurged for approximately 3
minutes and shut-in. The MUST actuator with pressure and temperature
gauges was then run. After latching onto the MUST valve, the well
was opened up for an initial flow for approximately 8 minutes. The
well was then shut-in for an initial build-up. After approximately 2
hrs shut-in, the well was opened up for the main flow. Approximately
one hour into the main flow the MUST signal was lost, but it was
decided to continue flowing the well without surface read out. (The
failure of the MUST was due to the wire being squeezed by one of the
slipjoints.)

During this flow periode samples, pressure and temperature readings
and flow rate measurements were taken as per programme.

The 9 5/8" casing was perforated at 170 m and cut at 340 m. The cut

pressure tested to 152 bar.

The anchors were retrieved up and the well was permanently left at
